attempts.prompt:
Create one finished character reference sheet, 1536x1024 pixels, landscape 3:2, a quiet warm ivory artist's folio. CHARACTER ONLY. Absolutely no locations, scenic vignette, furniture, floor plane, terrain, rocks, plants, window, decorative scenery, or prose paragraph. Plenty of clean ivory between isolated studies. Upper left readable elegant dark serif text exactly: "Coris" and below it "A Curse Before Breakfast". Brief functional labels only.
SUBJECT: one consistent adult human woman, exactly age twenty-one, ordinary anatomy, two arms two legs; dark brown long hair twisted up around one ordinary pencil, warm fair skin, brown eyes, expressive tired face with understated dry humor. She is an everyday contemporary-like witch and an older sister, not a fantasy-costume witch. No pointed hat, magical staff, amulet, armor, cloak, wand, spell glow or supernatural eyes. Default clothing: simple loose cream long-sleeve top, blue-gray loose vertically striped trousers, plain thick socks. Exact hair color, top and sock colors are restrained design choices; trousers and hair pencil are story facts.
LAYOUT: left two-thirds, three uncropped full-figure isolated views of SAME well woman in exactly same clothing and proportions: relaxed front three-quarter, clean side, rear three-quarter; all hair-to-sock silhouettes visible. Neutral natural relaxed hands. Keep pencil/bun placement and trouser stripe rhythm consistent. Right column: three compact expressive head/shoulder studies of SAME face, labels "Well", "Day ague", "Pencilled spots". Well: hair in pencil twist, faint wry expression. Day ague: flushed, tired watery eyes, several distinct round pea-green spots on bridge of nose and cheeks; wrapped at shoulders in muted teal quilt, no furniture. Pencilled spots: same adult wearing a plain dressing gown, clearly imperfect green oval and scratch-tailed cosmetic-pencil marks, mild mischievous look, not the neat round real spots. Bottom middle: small close study of long hair secured around the ordinary pencil, labelled "Hair pencil"; a single simple green cosmetic pencil labelled "Eye pencil"; unobtrusive five-stroke palette strip. No extra person, extra hand, story quotation or narrative scene.
PAINT: Canadian Group of Seven-inspired character painting in real heavy oil on ivory, broad connected color/value masses with directional bristle strokes and occasional substantial raised palette-knife impasto. Quiet connecting passages let silhouettes breathe. The same broad visibly painted treatment constructs cheeks, eyes, nose, hair and fingers as constructs fabricâ€”NO airbrushed or photoreal face inset. Paint follows actual form: long sweeping hair strokes, folds with a few decisive slabs, soft matte skin built from connected planes. Subdued neutral-warm illumination and rich cool slate-blue shadows, no theatrical rim light or high gloss. Warm cream, muted blue-gray, dark umber, teal, selective olive green. Enough impasto to feel physical, never a uniform layer of tiny beveled chips or all-over noisy mosaic. Natural readable features, not anime eyes.
INPUTS: image 1 is the approved Sculpted Impasto medium and folio approach only; borrow neither its character, red cloak, medieval equipment NOR its scenery. Image 2 is the story's oil-painted interior solely for slate/teal/cream palette and fabric paint rhythm; copy NONE of its objects, room, furniture, window, landscape or lighting composition. Strictly isolated character studies on untouched ivory, with no floor or setting.
